name: a0.dev
description: Mobile-first prompt-to-app builder. No public usage data.

name: Aider
description: The original git-native terminal pair programmer. Bring-your-own-key, no subscription.

name: Amp
default_model_note: Sourcegraph selects the model; billing is zero-markup pass-through rather than a seat price.
description: Sourcegraph's agent, sold as zero-markup pay-as-you-go with a free tier.

name: Augment Code
description: Context-engine-led IDE agent aimed at large existing codebases.

name: Base44
status_note: Acquired by Wix in 2025. Unlike most acquisitions in this category it kept growing after the deal — Wix put Base44 at roughly $150M ARR as of May 2026 in its own Q1 2026 results, and its Q2 2026 results (released 4 August 2026) still credit "strong Base44 performance" for group revenue up 15% year on year — so "acquired" here does not mean "avoid".
default_model_note: Wix announced it in its Q2 2026 results, released 4 August 2026: "Base44 becomes first app-creation platform to launch proprietary LLM — Base 1", which Wix says gives it "greater direct control over the largest cost driver in AI-native businesses, compute and inference spend" and takes Base44 from near-zero to roughly 60% non-GAAP gross margin in the second half. Wix does not publish which model serves an individual generation, so read this as the model the product now runs on rather than a per-request guarantee.
description: Prompt-to-app builder, now a Wix property, which Wix reported at roughly $150M ARR as of May 2026.

name: Bolt.new
status_note: Reached roughly $40M ARR in five months, then published no comparable 2026 milestone while Lovable kept compounding. Recorded as stalled on public momentum, not as dead.
description: In-browser prompt-to-app builder with native Stripe and Supabase wiring.

name: Claude Code
default_model_note: Bundled with the Claude subscription; also usable with an API key or through a gateway.
description: Anthropic's terminal coding agent. The highest-adoption CLI agent by developer survey share.

name: Cline
default_model_note: Bring-your-own key. Its real model mix is visible in OpenRouter usage rather than in any announcement.
description: The bring-your-own-key VS Code agent extension. Users pay providers directly, not Cline.

name: OpenAI Codex CLI
default_model_note: Bundled with ChatGPT plans; a dedicated higher tier exists for heavy usage.
description: OpenAI's open-source terminal coding agent, distributed through ChatGPT subscriptions.

name: Codex cloud tasks
description: Codex's hosted task runner, distributed through ChatGPT rather than sold separately.

name: Continue
status_note: continue.dev now reads "Continue has joined Cursor · Continue was acquired by Cursor" and the pricing page is gone. The Apache-2.0 repository is still public and was still being pushed to on 2 August 2026. No announcement date is published, so the date here is when it was first observed.
description: Open-source, configurable IDE assistant for VS Code and JetBrains. Acquired by Cursor; the open-source codebase remains available.

name: Cursor
default_model_note: Multi-model: Cursor routes across frontier models and its own Composer model rather than committing to one default.
description: VS Code fork built around whole-codebase agentic editing.

name: Devin
default_model_note: Not disclosed. Billed in ACUs (agent compute units), which is what makes cost-per-task comparisons hard.
description: The enterprise cloud agent. Priced in agent compute units rather than seats or tokens.

name: Factory AI
description: Enterprise "Droids" for delegated engineering work. No public revenue figures.

name: Figma Make
description: Figma’s in-canvas prompt-to-app feature, sold inside Figma seats.

name: Firebase Studio
status_note: firebase.studio carries a banner: "We're sunsetting Firebase Studio on March 22, 2027 so you can no longer create new workspaces. Move your code to Google AI Studio or Google Antigravity." Still usable until then, but it is not a tool to start a project on.
description: Google's agentic app workspace, wired to the Firebase backend. Sunsetting 22 March 2027.

name: Gemini CLI
status_note: Free consumer access ended 18 June 2026; users were directed to Google Antigravity. The tool still exists for API-key and paid use, so this is a withdrawn access tier rather than a shutdown — a distinction almost every ranked page gets wrong.
description: Google's open-source terminal agent. Consumer free tier withdrawn in June 2026.

name: GitHub Copilot
default_model_note: Model picker across OpenAI, Anthropic and Google models; the default has changed repeatedly and is not published as a stable fact.
description: The incumbent inline-completion and chat assistant, bundled into VS Code and the JetBrains IDEs.

name: Google Antigravity
default_model_note: Gemini-family default. Absorbed the Gemini CLI consumer base when free CLI access ended.
description: Google's agent-first IDE, and the destination Google pushed Gemini CLI's free users toward.

name: Jules
description: Google's asynchronous coding agent. Out of beta; no public usage numbers.

name: Kilo Code
default_model_note: Bring-your-own key or Kilo credits; no bundled default.
description: A merge-fork of Cline and Roo Code, and among the highest-volume coding tools on OpenRouter.

name: Kiro
description: Spec-driven agentic IDE from AWS: the agent writes requirements and design docs before code.

name: Lovable
default_model_note: Not disclosed. Credits, not tokens, are the billing unit.
description: Prompt-to-app builder that said it passed $200M ARR in November 2025. Supabase is the native backend default.

name: Magic Patterns
description: Prototyping tool aimed at product teams rather than engineers.

name: Onlook
description: Open-source visual editor that writes back into a real React codebase.

name: opencode
default_model_note: Provider-agnostic across 75+ providers; the user picks. This is why its model mix tracks price, not brand.
description: Provider-agnostic open-source terminal agent. The largest OSS star count in the ecosystem.

name: OpenRouter
description: The default bring-your-own-key routing layer, and the source of this project’s usage data.

name: Replit Agent
description: Prompt-to-app inside a full hosted development environment.

name: Roo Code
status_note: Repository archived 15 May 2026; the team pivoted to a separate product. It had roughly 1.56M installs at the point it stopped, which is why so many still-ranking "Cline vs Roo Code" pages now give an answer that cannot be acted on.
description: Archived VS Code agent extension. Large install base, development stopped.

name: Rork
description: Prompt-to-mobile-app builder on React Native and Expo.

name: Subframe
description: Design tool that ships an MCP server so coding agents can drive it directly.

name: Trae
description: ByteDance AI IDE. No credible independent usage data has been published.

name: v0
default_model_note: Vercel-hosted models; the composer model is not published as a stable identifier.
description: Vercel’s prompt-to-UI tool, distributed through the Vercel platform.

name: Vibecode
description: Mobile app builder with pluggable models and on-device testing over QR.

name: Windsurf
status_note: Acquired by Cognition in 2025 after the Google deal took the founding team; $82M ARR at acquisition. Every "Cursor vs Windsurf" page written before the acquisition describes a company that no longer exists independently.
description: Agent-first IDE, formerly Codeium. Now a Cognition property alongside Devin.

name: Zed
default_model_note: Bring-your-own key or Zed-hosted credits; no single bundled default.
description: Rust-native editor with an agent panel. Free to use, open source, paid hosted inference.
